Illustrative rows. Each row pairs one recording with its vowel.

speakerNotes: The rows shown are illustrative teaching examples, not a supplied dataset. Both complete matrices have 110 rows. Input columns are F1 and F2 in Hz. Output columns, in order, are done, dune, dean, Don, Dan. A 1 marks the true vowel. The third row, 320 and 2000 with target dean, matches the network example. The network shows the original pre-backpropagation activations; small weight labels are omitted in this compressed diagram. Files used on the next slide are assumed saved as PyTorch tensors using torch.save.

shapes.text: One gradient step using all 110 rows

speakerNotes: The program assumes Formant_Inputs.pt and TrueVowel_Outputs.pt already contain the two matrices saved as tensors with torch.save. The .float() calls ensure floating-point inputs and one-hot targets. Linear layers follow exactly 2→3→2→4→5. No hidden activation function is declared. The program uses PyTorch defaults for Linear layers. CrossEntropyLoss accepts logits and floating-point one-hot targets, performing the softmax-related loss calculation internally. The last five lines perform one full-batch SGD step, with learning rate 0.1 as requested. This is a minimal illustration, not a recommendation to repeatedly train on unscaled Hz values at that rate. The displayed network shows the prior illustrative hand-selected weights; the minimal program initializes its own parameters. Official references: https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.nn.CrossEntropyLoss.html and https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.nn.Linear.html and https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.optim.SGD.html

shapes.text: Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine, 1932

Neurons are nearly digital! On or off, roughly.
If the inner product is large positive, 
sigmoid function is near 1, and if inner product
Is large negative, sigmois is basically 0.

Animal perception reflects this: some things that seem 
alike, are perceived different, and some things that are
Very different are perceived same!

speakerNotes: Edgar Douglas Adrian shared the 1932 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine with Charles Sherrington. https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/medicine/1932/summary/-/ . The quotation is a 21-word excerpt from his lecture The Activity of the Nerve Fibres, December 12, 1932, reproduced on page 140 of Philippides, Husbands, Smith and O’Shea (2005), Flexible Couplings: Diffusing Neuromodulators and Adaptive Robotics. https://users.sussex.ac.uk/~philh/pubs/flexibleCouplingsPubl.pdf . The excerpt begins partway through a sentence, indicated by the ellipsis. Adrian described rate coding. This provides biological motivation for rate-based neuron models, not evidence that he invented the logistic sigmoid or that this precise sentence directly caused its adoption. The plotted logistic is a later mathematical model, not a fit to Adrian’s experimental data. Exact values: sigmoid(-4)=0.01798620996209156 and sigmoid(4)=0.9820137900379085.

shapes.text: Applying sigmoid, one neuron at a time
Purple: linear activation     Green: sigmoid activation
Inputs stay as formants. Downstream values recalculate; outputs use softmax.
Initially: all hidden activations are linear.

speakerNotes: Nine clicks sigmoid the nine hidden neurons in layer order: 3, then 2, then 4. Inputs are unchanged. Every stage uses the same original weights, no biases, and recomputes all downstream preactivations and output probabilities. Purple neurons remain linear. Green neurons have sigmoid applied after their inner product. This progression constructs the sigmoid network, rather than simply applying sigmoid to the stored outputs of a different all-linear network. Outputs remain softmax, matching multiclass cross-entropy. Full stage data is calculated at full precision; values on slide are rounded to 3 decimals.

shapes.text: The same PyTorch program, with sigmoid

speakerNotes: The earlier program is repeated with nn.Sigmoid() inserted after Linear(2,3), Linear(3,2), and Linear(2,4). Linear(4,5) outputs logits for CrossEntropyLoss, which handles the softmax-related loss calculation. SGD learning rate is still 0.1. Source: https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/2.14/generated/torch.nn.Sigmoid.html . The diagram uses the original illustrative weights and no biases; the minimal PyTorch declarations use their default initialization and options. Input files must exist and have shapes 110x2 and 110x5.
